Finding a replacement jar that actually fits the same lid turns into a weird scavenger hunt, because "standard" sizing is more of a suggestion than a rule. The headache usually comes down to thread dimensions and mouth diameter, not aesthetics. Ball and Kerr canning jars, for example, follow a Regular Mouth finish at 70 mm and a Wide Mouth finish at 86 mm, per manufacturer documentation. As of 2026, most jars on the market still cluster around those two standards, but specialty terrarium vessels like Weck, apothecary, and geometric glass use their own thread pitches. Match the wrong one and the lid either won't seat or won't seal. Once you know your lid's measurements, the sourcing part is straightforward. Quick Answer Measure the lid's outer thread diameter with a ruler or caliper first. Most terrarium jars use either 70 mm Regular Mouth or 86 mm Wide Mouth canning threads. Match those numbers to a replacement jar with the same finish from Ball, Kerr, Bernardin, Weck, or a custom glassmaker. Buy a jar only, a lid only, or a full bundle depending on which piece is missing.
